en: Noble homage to Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta! The Supreme Praise of Mañjuśrījñānasattva: A Liturgical Hymn Entitled "The Lamp of Wisdom. Homage to the Noble One, Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta! In the language of India: Ārya-mañjuśrījñānasattvasya-paramārtha-nāma-saṃgīti. In the language of Tibet: ’Phags pa ’jam dpal ye shes sems dpa’i don dam pa’i mtshan yang dag par brjod pa. Homage to the Noble One, Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta! I prostrate to the Lord of Sages, the supreme among beings, To the one who possesses the ten powers, the Great Sage, To the one who has transcended all states of existence, To the one who is the embodiment of the three bodies (trikāya). Homage to the one who is the nature of all phenomena, To the one who is the primordial wisdom of all Buddhas, To the one who is the source of all mantras, To the one who is the essence of all tantras. Homage to the one who is the great king of mantras, To the one who is the sovereign of all vidyās, To the one who is the supreme lord of secrets, To the one who is the master of the three realms. Homage to the one who is the great physician, To the one who cures the disease of ignorance, To the one who bestows the medicine of wisdom, To the one who leads to the city of liberation. Homage to the one who is the great hero, To the one who subdues the hosts of Māras, To the one who grants fearlessness to all beings, To the one who is the protector of the world. Homage to the one who is the great sage, To the one who is the knower of all things, To the one who is the teacher of the Dharma, To the one who is the guide to the path of peace. May this supreme praise of the noble Mañjuśrījñānasattva, Which is the treasury of all the Buddhas’ intentions, Be accomplished for the benefit of all sentient beings, And may it swiftly bring about the state of omniscience. Thus ends the Supreme Praise of Mañjuśrījñānasattva, the Liturgical Hymn entitled "The Lamp of Wisdom. May it be auspicious!

ṭhaḥiitd: Āryamañjuśrīnāmasaṃgīti. For my benefit, for my sake, and out of compassion for me, O All-Pervading Lord, may I attain the perfect awakening of the Net of Illusion (Māyājālābhisaṃbodhi).

For the sake of all sentient beings who are submerged in the mire of ignorance and whose minds are agitated by the afflictions, may the Blessed One, the Teacher, the World-Guru, the Perfectly Awakened One— who knows the reality of the great *samaya* and is supreme in knowing the dispositions of the faculties— proclaim the *Āryamañjuśrīnāmasaṃgīti*. [He proclaims it] for the Blessed One, the Great Uṣṇīṣa, the Lord of Speech, Mañjuśrī-jñānasattva, the self-arisen embodiment of primordial wisdom.
The *Nāmasaṅgīti*, supreme, profound in meaning, noble in meaning, of great meaning, peerless, auspicious, and virtuous in the beginning, middle, and end—

this has been spoken by the Buddhas of the past, will be spoken by those of the future, and is spoken again and again by the perfectly awakened ones of the present. It is that which is chanted within this *Māyājāla* Great Tantra by the joyful, immeasurable holders of mantra who are Great Vajradharas.

I pray that you explain that which was joyfully proclaimed by the Immeasurables. With firm resolve, I shall uphold this until the end of cyclic existence, O Protector, so that I may become a holder of the secrets of all the Perfect Buddhas. Thus he spoke.
Until I have attained definitive emergence, I shall uphold this with firm intention.

I shall reveal it to sentient beings according to the particularity of their inclinations, for the sake of destroying all afflictions without exception and for the sake of abandoning all ignorance without exception; I shall explain it thoroughly, in accordance with the specific dispositions of sentient beings.
I too shall uphold this; with firm intention, may I emerge in renunciation. How may I become a holder of the secrets of all the Protectors, the Perfect Buddhas?

Thus it is said: The Blessed Buddha, the Perfectly Awakened One, is born from the syllable *A*.
The syllable *A* is the foremost of all letters, of great significance, and the supreme syllable.

Joyful and delighted, with palms joined, they prostrated to the Protector, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the Perfect Buddha.
And by many other lords, the Indras of Secrets, the Vajrapāṇis, and others as well.
The many other protectors, as well as Guhyapati Vajrapāṇi together with the kings of the wrathful deities— by all of them, [may there be protection].
From the *Guhyastuti*, this verse was offered:
"O Protector, we rejoice! Excellent, excellent is this well-spoken [teaching]. A great benefit has been bestowed upon us, which brings about perfect awakening."
O Protector, we rejoice;
excellent, excellent, well spoken! May we [attain] the perfectly complete...
He performs the great purpose of attaining enlightenment;
for this world which is without a protector and yearns for the fruit of liberation, this pure path to excellence has been proclaimed through the method of the Net of Illusion.
This pure and excellent path, which reveals the manner of the *Māyājāla*, is for those beings who are without a protector and for those who seek the fruit of complete liberation.
Profound, vast, and extensive, of great significance, and accomplishing the welfare of the world—this is indeed the domain of the Buddhas, taught by the Perfectly Enlightened One.
Profound, vast, and extensive, Of great significance, it accomplishes the welfare of beings;
This is the domain of the Buddhas.
"Expounded by all the perfect Buddhas.

Thus ends the *Paramārthanāmasaṃgīti* of the Blessed One Mañjuśrījñānasattva, spoken by the Blessed Tathāgata Śākyamuni. Following this verse, D. 13b.4 states: "These are the five verses that summarize the authentic exhortation."
This does not occur in the *Gandavyūha*, from the chapter on the Net of Samādhis in the sixteen-thousand-verse [version].
The *Āryamañjuśrīnāmasaṃgīti*, the Chanting of the Names of Noble Mañjuśrī, spoken by the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, is complete.

This was excellently translated and edited by the monk Blo gros brtan pa (Sthiramati), a translator of the revised terminology who was nurtured by the kindness of the Great Being, the holy Guru Chos kyi rgyal po (Dharmarāja), who had attained mastery over all the common and uncommon scriptures,
at the secluded hermitage of Sam gling.
Although these great scholars of old have repeatedly transmitted this tantra and it is indeed renowned to all,
nevertheless, the meaning is exactly as it is in the scriptures.
This tantra was excellently translated by the second Sthiramati. For those seekers who strive for the wisdom of the definitive meaning of the profound and vast Vajrayāna,
yet do not rely properly upon the Dharma and its meaning—

O person, do not follow after the mere words and syllables! O Vajrapāṇi, O Vajradhara, this is the *Nāmasaṅgīti*—the unique and perfectly pure [recitation] of the Blessed One Mañjuśrī-jñānasattva, who is the embodiment of wisdom and the body of all-knowledge. It has been taught, proclaimed, released, analyzed, revealed, and empowered by me for the sake of generating unsurpassed joy, delight, and great rapture; for the purification of the secrets of body, speech, and mind; for the fulfillment and purification of the accumulations of merit and wisdom on the stages and perfections that were previously incomplete and impure; for the attainment of the meaning not yet attained, and for the further realization of what has already been attained; and for the purpose of upholding the system of the true Dharma of all the Tathāgatas. O Vajrapāṇi, O Vajradhara, this has been empowered within your continuum by my empowerment through the nature of all mantras. These are the eleven verses of benefit for the first cycle. Furthermore, O Vajrapāṇi, O Vajradhara, this *Nāmasaṅgīti* is utterly pure, purified as the secret of the body, speech, and mind of the Omniscient One. It is the awakening (*bodhi*) of all Tathāgatas; the direct realization (*abhisamaya*) of the Perfectly Awakened Ones; the unsurpassed state of all Tathāgatas; the course of the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) of all Sugatas; the defeat of the forces of all Māras by the Victors; the essence of the ten powers of all those possessing the ten powers; omniscience of the Omniscient One; the source of all knowledges; the arrival at all phenomena; the equal realization of all Buddhas; the fulfillment of the stainless and utterly pure accumulations of merit and wisdom of all Mahābodhisattvas; the birth of all Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas; the perfect field of all gods and humans; the foundation of the Mahāyāna; the origin of the conduct of Bodhisattvas; the culmination of the noble path; the examination of liberations; the arising of the path of departure; the non-interruption of the lineage of the Tathāgatas; the growth of the family and clan of the great Bodhisattvas; the subjugation of all opponents; the destruction of all heretics; the defeat of the armies and hosts of the four Māras; the gathering of all sentient beings; the ripening of the noble path for all who travel toward liberation; the meditative absorption (*samādhi*) of those dwelling in the four divine abodes (*brahmavihāra*); the dhyāna of those with one-pointed minds; the yoga of those engaged in body, speech, and mind; the dissociation from all fetters; the abandonment of all primary and secondary afflictions (*kleśa-upakleśa*); the pacification of all obscurations; the liberation from all bonds; the release from all remainders; the peace of all mental disturbances; the mine of all prosperities; the avoidance of all misfortunes; the closing of the doors to all lower realms; the true path to the city of liberation; the cessation of the wheel of saṃsāra; the turning of the wheel of Dharma; the raising of the parasol, banner, and flag of the Tathāgata’s teaching; the empowerment of the teaching of the True Dharma; and the swift accomplishment of the Bodhisattva’s attainment of mantras.

[He is] the progenitor of those who have entered the conduct of the gates [of practice], the realization through meditation of those devoted to the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), and the contemplation of emptiness and the cultivation of non-dual contemplation for those devoted to such practice;
he is the father of the entire host of all the perfections (*pāramitā*).
The completion of all the perfectly pure stages and perfections;
the contemplation of the fourfold ultimate truth;
the contemplation of all phenomena as one; and the four foundations of mindfulness.
This *Nāmasaṅgīti* is the fulfillment of all the qualities of a Buddha; such is the detailed explanation. These are the fifty-two words of praise for the second wheel.
Furthermore, Vajrapāṇi, O Holder of the Vajra, this *Nāmasaṅgīti* effects the pacification of all sins committed by the body, speech, and mind of all sentient beings;
it is the purification of all miserable states of existence for all beings and the warding off of all evil destinies.
It is the cutting off of all karmic obscurations,
the non-arising of all that is produced during the eight inopportune states,
and the pacification of the eight great fears.
It is the dispelling of all bad dreams, the removal of all ill omens,
and the pacification of all adverse signs and obstacles.
It is the distancing of all the activities of the enemy Māra,
the increasing of all roots of virtue and merits,
and the non-arising of all improper mental attentions.
It is the uprooting of all intoxication, pride, arrogance, and egoism; it is the non-arising of all suffering and mental distress;
it is the essence of all Tathāgatas.
It is the secret of all bodhisattvas,
the great secret of all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, and the essence of all mudrās and mantras.

It brings about the arising of mindfulness and clear comprehension; it makes the eloquence of supreme wisdom for those who proclaim all dharmas as inexpressible; and it effects the perfection of health, strength, and sovereignty.
It is the furtherance of prosperity, auspiciousness, peace, and welfare;
the manifestation of fame, renown, glory, and praise;
and the pacification of all fears of great diseases, which are utterly pure and most purified.
It is the most pure of the pure,
the most prosperous of the prosperous,
and the most auspicious of the auspicious.
He is the refuge for those seeking refuge, the state for those without a state,
and the protection for those seeking protection.
He is the kinsman of those without kin;
he is an island for those seeking an island; he is the unsurpassed refuge for those without refuge. *The Noble Mañjuśrī-nāmasaṃgīti*.
She has become a boat for those crossing to the further shore of the ocean of existence;
she has become a great sovereign physician for the eradication of all diseases;
and she has become wisdom for the discernment of things to be abandoned and things to be adopted.

Having become the light of knowledge for the purpose of dispelling the darkness of all false views; having become a wish-fulfilling gem for the purpose of fulfilling the aspirations and desires of all sentient beings according to their inclinations;
and having become the omniscient wisdom for the purpose of attaining the wisdom-body of Mañjuśrī.
It has become the vision of perfectly pure gnosis for the sake of attaining the five eyes;
it has become the fulfillment of the six perfections through the bestowing of the gift of material goods, fearlessness, and the Dharma;
and it has become the means for reaching the ten stages through the complete fulfillment of the accumulations of merit, gnosis, and meditative concentration.
The non-dual nature of phenomena is for the purpose of removing duality;
suchness is its intrinsic nature, and it is the nature of no other phenomenon, which serves to remove superimpositions.

Its nature as the *dharmadhātu* is, by virtue of being the purified body of gnosis of all Tathāgatas, the nature of the great emptiness in all its aspects, through the total rejection of the thicket of all false views.
Since all phenomena are ineffable, that which is the *Nāmasaṃgīti*—namely, the name-recitation—is for the purpose of maintaining and revealing the meaning of non-dual reality (*advayadharmatā*).
Thus, these are the fifty-two words of praise for the third wheel.

Furthermore, Vajrapāṇi, O Vajradhara, whichever son of noble family or daughter of noble family, practicing the conduct of the mantra-path among the Bodhisattvas, shall daily, at the three times of day, uphold, recite, master, and propagate this *Nāmasaṅgīti*—the crest-jewel named the *Nāmasaṅgīti* of the Blessed One Mañjuśrī-jñānasattva, the non-dual ultimate reality, the embodiment of wisdom of all Tathāgatas, and the Blessed One’s form of gnosis—using these very verses, phrases, and syllables in their entirety, complete and unbroken, through the thorough understanding of the profound movement [of the Dharma].
He will correctly attend to it with proper mental engagement,
and he will explain it in detail to others according to the occasion, up to its full revelation;
and for the sake of directly realizing the activity of Mañjuśrī’s gnosis through the meaning of any one of the various names, he will cultivate it with a one-pointed mind.

By means of both mental engagement with resolute conviction and mental engagement with reality, he dwells in the "all-encompassing gateway" (samantamukha-vihāra). Endowed with supreme, unclouded faith that penetrates through wisdom, all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the three times and the timelessness will gather and assemble before him, and they will reveal and manifest all the gateways of the Dharma.
Through the empowerment of all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, they will correctly empower his continuum with body, speech, and mind.
By means of the favor bestowed by all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas,
they will be graced with favor and will achieve eloquence and fearlessness regarding all dharmas.
The Pratyekabuddhas will manifest the existence of the noble Dharma;

and the Great Wrathful Kings, such as Mahāvajradhara—the tamers of those difficult to subdue, who have become the protectors of the world—will, through their various emanation-bodies, demonstrate vigor, strength, splendor, and invincibility, and they will instruct upon all the mantra-seals, realizations, and mandalas.

All the kings of mantras and spells without exception, as well as those who are invincible to all great obstacles, Vināyakas, Māras, enemies, and adversaries, will protect, rescue, and guard [the practitioner] day and night, at every moment, in all activities and on all paths.

Brahmā, Indra, Upendra, Rudra, Nārāyaṇa, all the Kumāras, Maheśvara, Kārttikeya, Mahākāla, Rāmeśvara, Yama, Varuṇa, Kubereśvara, and whoever are the world-protectors of the ten directions—all of them, at all times and continuously, day and night, whether walking, standing, sitting, reclining, sleeping, waking, in meditative concentration or non-concentration, in a single state or moving among many people, and as far as their dwelling in villages, towns, market-towns, districts, provinces, royal palaces, gate-pins, turrets, roads, paths, crossroads, triple junctions, the interior of cities, or the midst of markets—[all these shall protect this Dharma discourse].

As long as they enter empty houses, mountain wildernesses, rivers, cemeteries, thickets, and forests, they will always, in every way, supremely protect, guard, and preserve the lives of all beings— whether defiled or undefiled, intoxicated or joyful— and day and night they will perform what is most auspicious.
Furthermore, those gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans;

and furthermore, those planets, lunar mansions, the group of Mothers, Gaṇapati, the Seven Mothers, and the yakṣīs, rākṣasīs, and piśācīs—all of them, together with their retinues and their respective classes, will provide supreme protection, preservation, and guardianship on the paths and roads of his conduct;
moreover, they will instill splendor and strength within his body.
They shall also bring about the increase of health, strength, and longevity.
These are the nineteen items concerning the benefits of the fourth wheel.

Furthermore, Vajrapāṇi, O Vajradhara, whoever takes up this *Nāmasaṅgīti*, known as the "Crest Jewel," every day without fail, and having committed it to memory, recites it three times, or having made it into a book, reads or proclaims the *Āryamañjuśrīnāmasaṅgīti*, while relying upon the form of the Blessed One Mañjuśrījñānasattva and contemplating that form—by meditating upon that form, and by swiftly acquiring the power to discipline beings through the body of the emanation of reality (*tattvanirmāṇarūpakāya*), he shall behold him.

That mahāsattva will see all the various emanation-form bodies of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas present together, even as they sit in the expanse of the sky; and although he is born into this world, he will have no fear of falling into the miserable states or the lower realms,
nor will he be born into a low family.
He will not be born in a border region;
he will not have dull faculties;
he will not have impaired faculties.
He will not be born into a family of wrong views;
he will not be born in Buddha-fields that are not sustained by the empowerment of a Buddha;
and the arising of a Buddha and the Dharma taught by him will never be abandoned nor will they ever be out of his sight.
He will not be born among the long-lived gods;
he will not be born during the aeons of famine, disease, and weapons;
he will not be born during the times of the five corruptions.
There will be no fear of kings, thieves, or enemies;
there will be no fear of all calamities, poverty, or destitution;
and there will be no fear of lack of praise, slander, insult, censure, ill-repute, or infamy.
He will be endowed with a noble birth, family, and lineage; he will be universally beautiful and possessed of excellent form and complexion;
he will be beloved and heart-pleasing to worldly people, supremely pleasant in association, and dear to behold.
Among worldly people, he will be handsome, fortunate, and one whose words are accepted;
wherever he is born, there he will remember his past lives;
and he will possess great wealth and a large retinue, with inexhaustible wealth and an inexhaustible retinue.
He will be endowed with the knowledge of the supreme vows of all sentient beings;
by his very nature, he will be endowed with the qualities of the six perfections,
and he will dwell in the four divine abodes.
Endowed with the power of the means of mindfulness and clear comprehension, as well as with aspiration and knowledge,
he will become confident in all treatises, skillful in debate, and possessed of a clear, unconfused, and radiant intellect.
He will be skillful, untiring, knowledgeable in the ritual procedures, possessed of great purpose, and free from craving;
he will become a teacher most trustworthy to all sentient beings, worthy of honor, and a venerable master.
Furthermore, all the previously unheard treatises on arts, mathematics, and sciences will become perfectly clear to him in both their meaning and their established tenets.
He will be endowed with extremely pure morality, livelihood, conduct, and behavior; he will be one who has truly gone forth and is correctly ordained;
through the *Āryamañjuśrīnāmasaṃgīti*, there will be no forgetting of omniscience and the mind of awakening (*bodhicitta*).
One will never abide in the fixed course of the Śrāvaka, Arhat, or Pratyekabuddha.
These fifty-one words constitute the benefit of the fifth wheel.
Thus, O Vajrapāṇi, O Vajradhara, he will be endowed with immeasurable qualities; he will be endowed with such other immeasurable qualities as these.

O Vajrapāṇi, O Vajradhara, any person who upholds this *Paramārthanāmasaṅgīti* will, after quickly accumulating the equipment of merit and wisdom, very swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

For many eons, he will remain by means of the nature of non-extinction and become a King of Dharma, empowered as the great drum of Dharma in the ten directions, the unsurpassed teacher of Dharma for all sentient beings.
This is the immeasurable benefit of the sixth wheel.
Vajrapāṇi,
the Vajradhara—
this is the wisdom body (*jñānakāya*) of the Blessed One.

This is the *Mañjuśrī-jñānasattva-asambhinna-pariśuddha-nāma-saṃgīti*, the perfect recitation of the names of the wisdom-body of all the Tathāgatas and the utterly pure, unmixed [qualities] of Mañjuśrī-jñānasattva;
it is for the purpose of perfectly generating in you unsurpassed joy, rapture, and great delight.
Because the secrets of body, speech, and mind are completely pure,
and because the stages, the perfections, and the accumulations of merit and primordial wisdom— which were previously incomplete and impure— are now fully perfected.
For the sake of complete purification;
for the sake of further realizing the unsurpassed meaning that was not previously realized;
and for the sake of attaining what had not been attained.
Furthermore, for the sake of correctly upholding the way of the sublime Dharma of all the Tathāgatas, I shall proclaim it, perfectly and thoroughly explain it,
and fully elucidate it.
It is that which has been analyzed, elucidated,
and blessed.
Vajrapāṇi, Vajradhara,
this [teaching] has been blessed within your continuum by the blessing of the entire reality (dharmatā) of mantra.
These are the eleven praises following the first turning of the wheel.
Furthermore, Vajrapāṇi,
this *Vajradhara-nāmasaṃgīti* is utterly pure and completely refined;
it constitutes the secret of the body, speech, and mind of omniscient primordial wisdom.
This is the awakening of the buddhahood of all the Tathāgatas.
It is the clear realization of the perfectly complete Buddhas;
it is the unsurpassed [teaching] of all the Tathāgatas.
It is the realization of the dharmadhātu of all the Sugatas.
It is that which defeats all the powers of Māra of the Victors;
it has become the power of the ten powers of all those who possess the ten powers.
It is the omniscience of all the primordial wisdoms of the Omniscient One.
It is the oral transmission of all phenomena;
it is the perfect and complete realization of all Buddhas.
This is the complete perfection of the accumulations of merit and primordial wisdom, which are stainless and utterly pure for all bodhisattva mahāsattvas. *Āryamañjuśrīnāmasaṃgīti*
It is the source from which all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas arise;
it is the field of excellence for all gods and humans.
This is the consecration of the Mahāyāna.
It is the source of the bodhisattva’s conduct;
it is the ultimate culmination of the noble path.
An Examination of Those Who Are Liberated.
It is the generation of the path of definitive emergence;
it is the non-interruption of the lineage of the Tathāgatas.
It causes the lineage and continuum of the great bodhisattvas to flourish and increase.
It is the subduer of all adversaries;
it is the total vanquisher of all non-Buddhist extremists.
It is that which defeats the power, the forces, and the hosts of the four māras.
It is the perfect gathering of all sentient beings.
It is the samādhi of those who abide in the four Brahmā-vihāras, through which the Noble Path of all vehicles is fully matured by means of definitive emergence.
This is the meditative concentration of those with one-pointed minds.
It is the yoga of those who apply themselves intensely with body, speech, and mind;
it is the freedom from all fetters of every kind of correct application.
It is the abandonment of all primary afflictions and secondary afflictions.
The complete pacification of all obscurations;
the total liberation from all bonds.
It is the liberation from all remaining [afflictions].
It is the pacification of all mental distractions and the source of all prosperity.
It utterly destroys all forms of decline.
It is the covering of all doors to the lower realms;
it is the sublime path to the city of complete liberation.
It is the non-entrance into the wheel of saṃsāra.
It is the thorough turning of the wheel of Dharma;
it is the raising aloft the parasol, victory banner, and pennant of the Tathāgata’s teaching.
It is the supreme abiding that teaches the sublime Dharma;
it is the swift accomplishment for those who practice the application of the gateway of mantra of the bodhisattvas.
It is the superior realization of the meditation of those who apply themselves to the perfections of wisdom.
It is the realization of emptiness by those who apply themselves to the meditation on non-dual discernment;
it is the generator of all the perfections and all the accumulations.
It is the complete perfection of all the thoroughly pure stages and perfections.
It is the individual discernment of the four authentic noble truths;
it is the individual discernment of all phenomena as one through the four applications of mindfulness.
This *Chanting of the Names of the Noble Mañjuśrī* is the complete perfection of all the qualities of a Buddha.
Furthermore, Vajrapāṇi,
this *Vajradhara-nāmasaṃgīti* is that which completely pacifies, without exception, all the misdeeds committed by the body, speech, and mind of all sentient beings.
It completely purifies all the lower realms of all sentient beings;
it averts all rebirths in the miserable states.
It completely severs all karmic obscurations.
It prevents all rebirths in the eight states of non-leisure from occurring;
it pacifies the eight great fears.
It definitively dispels all evil dreams.
It completely dispels all evil signs;
it thoroughly pacifies all ill omens and obstacles.
It keeps all the activities of the enemy Māra at a great distance;
it causes all roots of virtue and merit to increase and flourish.
It causes all improper mental engagements (*ayoniśo-manasikāra*) to not arise.
It utterly destroys all forms of gluttony, pride, arrogance, and ego-clinging;
it prevents all suffering and mental unease from arising.
Likewise, it has become the essence of all the Tathāgatas. *Āryamañjuśrīnāmasaṃgīti*
It is the secret of all bodhisattvas;
it is the great secret of all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.
He has become all mudrās and mantras.
It perfectly generates mindfulness and situational awareness for those who proclaim that all phenomena are inexpressible;
it brings about unsurpassed wisdom and mental acuity.
It brings about the perfection of health, strength, and sovereign power.
It causes glory, virtue, peace,
and excellence to increase greatly.
It makes fame, renown, verses of praise, and eulogies clearly manifest;
it brings all illnesses and great fears to an end.
It is that which brings about peace;
it is the ultimate purity of those who are utterly pure; it is the ultimate cleanliness of those who are utterly clean.
The most prosperous among the very prosperous;
the most auspicious among the very auspicious;
the refuge for those seeking protection.
He is the dwelling place for those without a dwelling;
he is the protector for those who desire protection;
he is the refuge for those without a refuge.
He has become an island for those who desire an island;
he has become an unsurpassed refuge for those who are without refuge;
[he has crossed] to the far shore of the ocean of existence.
He has become a boat for all wandering beings.
He has become the Great King of Physicians in order to definitively overcome all diseases. He has become wisdom in order to distinguish between things to be adopted and things to be abandoned.
In order to dispel all the thick darkness of evil views, it has become the light of primordial wisdom (*jñāna*).
In order to completely fulfill the intentions and desires of all sentient beings exactly as they are, it has become a wish-fulfilling jewel (*cintāmaṇi*).
Because he has fully attained the wisdom-body of Mañjuśrī, he has become the wisdom of omniscience.
Because he has fully attained the five eyes, he has become one who perceives with completely pure wisdom.
By means of perfectly bestowing the gifts of material things, fearlessness, and the Dharma, he has brought the six perfections to full completion.
By means of the complete perfection of the accumulations of merit and wisdom, as well as meditative concentration, the ten stages (bhūmis) are fully attained.
Because it is free from the phenomena of duality, it is the non-dual dharmatā.
Because it is particularly free from superimposition, it is the dharmatā that is not other than the nature of suchness.
By its very nature as the completely pure wisdom-body (*jñānakāya*) of all the Tathāgatas, it is the very nature of the ultimate reality (*bhūtakoṭi*).
By its very nature of definitively dispelling the entire nest of evil views without exception, it is the very nature of the great emptiness of all aspects.
This *Mañjuśrīnāmasaṃgīti* thus clearly elucidates the correct apprehension of both the names and the meaning of the non-dual dharmatā; therefore, all phenomena are inexpressible.
These are the fifty-two verses of praise following the third wheel.
Furthermore, Vajrapāṇi, Vajradhara,
any son of noble family or daughter of noble family who practices the conduct of the gateway of mantra—

This *Chakshurnorbu* (Cūḍāmaṇi), titled "The Perfect Expression of the Names of Ultimate Reality, the Non-dual Wisdom Body of all Tathāgatas, the Wisdom Body of the Blessed One Mañjuśrī Jñānasattva," is here presented in its entirety and complete perfection.
Without deficiency,
not fragmentary,
and in verse.
By means of these very words and syllables, they should daily, at the three times of day, uphold them, recite them,
master them,
and attend to them correctly.
Furthermore, one should clearly elucidate [the meaning] for others as well, extensively and exactly according to the occasion;
and for each of the various other meanings of the names, one should manifest the wisdom-body (*jñānakāya*) of Mañjuśrī and dwell in the state of the "abiding in all doors" with one-pointed mind.
The individual discernment of all phenomena,
the supreme,
and the stainless.
For one who penetrates through wisdom and proceeds correctly through faith,
all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the three times— without distinction of time— will truly assemble, truly approach, and truly arrive before them, and will reveal the gateways to all phenomena.
It teaches the cultivation of oneself;
through the blessings of all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, it perfectly blesses the continuum of one’s body, speech, and mind;
and through the care of all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, it provides protection.

They also bring about the eloquence of fearlessness regarding all phenomena. All Arhats, Śrāvakas, and Pratyekabuddhas, through their very intention of cherishing the noble Dharma, even offer up their own persons. Furthermore, those who subdue the difficult-to-tame [beings] appear as great wrathful kings.

The emanation bodies (*nirmāṇakāya*) of various forms, such as the Great Vajradhara and others who provide complete protection for all wandering beings, cannot be overwhelmed by [his] radiance, power, and majesty; they reveal the mantras, mudrās, visualizations (*abhisamaya*), and maṇḍalas,
as well as all the kings of mantras and vidyās without exception.
All obstacles, misleading spirits, māras, adversaries, and great invincible enemies— throughout both night and day, at every single moment in all their activities, and on all paths,
in streets and in places of refuge—
They conceal it.

Furthermore, Vajrapāṇi, Vajradhara,
this so-called *Nāmasaṃgīti*, the "Crown Jewel," should be correctly undertaken every single day without fail.
Reciting it from memory three times while residing at the throat, reading it as contained in a volume, and reciting it aloud;
By focusing on the form of the Bhagavān Mañjuśrī Jñānasattva, contemplating that form,
and meditating in dhyāna upon that form, one will— taking the capacity of those to be trained as the condition— behold him in his very own emanated form-body (nirmāṇakāya) before long.
One will also see all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas dwelling together in the expanse of space, abiding in various emanated form bodies. Furthermore,
no matter how that Great Being is born, they will never fall into the lower realms.
The fear of falling into the lower realms will not arise;
one will not be born into a low caste; and one will not become a person in a remote borderland.
One’s faculties will not become inferior; one’s faculties will not be incomplete.
They will not be born into families with wrong views.
They will not be born in buddhafields where no Buddha resides.
They will never be separated from the appearance of a Buddha or the Dharma he has taught, nor will they ever reject them.
One will not be born among the long-lived gods. One will not be born during the eons of famine, disease, and weapons. One will not be born during the times of the five degenerations.
Fear of kings, robbers, and enemies will not arise.
All fears of misfortune and poverty will not arise. [Nor will there be] ill repute...
Censuring, disparaging, and speaking unpleasantly;
The fear of an ill reputation will not arise.
